effect_mechanism: Water harvesting changes farm and programme costs in both directions. Practices that replace tillage save money: in Ghana farmers saved about half the cost of land preparation by switching to zero tillage with residue retention, which also had lower labour costs; in Mozambique labour costs were $153 per hectare for basins against $173 for conventional tillage; no-till with a residue mulch reduced total variable costs by 5% against conventional tillage in Zimbabwe; and mulching reduced weed density and labour costs for weeding in Ethiopia [ev_project_cost_dalt14_5, ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. Better siting saves on construction: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures, so works cost INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the conventional programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]. Practices that add earthworks or bought materials raise costs: switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, increased the cost of production in Ghana's Nandom area, and in Kenya the extra labour and plastic sheet made the total input value of film-mulched ridge-furrows 89.9 and 94.1% greater than flat planting [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2, ev_project_cost_mo17_8]. On the saving side: in Karnataka, planning structures from a land-resource inventory cut construction cost to INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the comparison programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; in Mozambique, labour for the basin practice averaged $153 against $173 per hectare under conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]; in Zimbabwe no-till systems cut total variable costs by 5% (with dead mulch) to 37.4% [ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5]; in Ethiopia mulching reduced labour costs for weeding [ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]; and in northwestern Ghana farmers saved about half the cost of land preparation by switching to conservation agriculture [ev_project_cost_dalt14_5]. On the cost side: in the same Ghanaian trials, switching from flat-land production to tied ridges with or without grass strips increased the cost of production [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]; in Kenya, ridge-furrows with plastic film raised the value of total inputs by 89.9 and 94.1% because of extra labour and plastic purchase [ev_project_cost_mo17_8]; and in Ghana most rehabilitated small dams cost USD 5,000 or more per irrigated hectare, with only 25% of government and 12% of donor-rehabilitated dams below that [ev_project_cost_veno12_1].

Several saving units are conservation-agriculture tillage contrasts, so they say more about tillage than about water capture, and the Kenyan cost rise is driven partly by plastic film, which is not nature-based. The Karnataka saving is a planning-efficiency comparison between programmes rather than a with-and-without contrast, and the Ghana dam costs are thresholds from a review rather than a comparison with an alternative. For scoping, expect labour savings from in-field moisture practices and added establishment costs for built structures.

effect_mechanism: Water-harvesting and conservation practices both cut and raise the cost of production, depending on what they replace. Practices that drop ploughing cut costs: zero tillage with residue retention in Ghana saved farmers about half the cost of land preparation and had lower labour costs than conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_dalt14_5], basins in Mozambique cost $153 per hectare in labour against $173 for conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5], and no-till with a dead mulch in Zimbabwe cut total variable costs by 5% [ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5]. Practices that build structures add cost: switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, raised the cost of production at Nandom in Ghana [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2], and ridge-furrow planting with film mulch in Kenya raised the value of total inputs by 89.9% and 94.1% over flat planting because of extra labour and plastic sheeting [ev_project_cost_mo17_8].
conditionality: What separates the sides is whether the practice removes tillage work or adds construction and materials: savings come from skipping land preparation, extra cost from building ridges and buying film. For a Task Team Leader, an in-field capture practice that replaces ploughing can lower running costs, while the same kind of practice added on top of ploughing raises them. The Ghana and Zimbabwe savings are for conservation agriculture without a capture structure, the Mozambique basins bundle basin digging with reduced tillage, and the Kenyan cost rise is driven partly by the plastic film [ev_project_cost_dalt14_5, ev_project_cost_mash25h1_5, ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_mo17_8].
